transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date: 2027-03-02
- Start time: 15:30 PT
- Duration: ~43 minutes
- Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Omar (Redwood SE), Lena (CSM), Marcus (Clearline), Sofia (Clearline), Priya (Clearline security), Ethan (Clearline PM)

Auto summary (auto-generated, may be rough):
Redwood and Clearline reviewed the weekend degradation (spike of 5xxs and increased timeouts) during a patient-data ingest peak. Team discussed root causes (burst > rate-window, KV cache coldness on model switch, LPs at the LB), proposed mitigations (adaptive backpressure, client-side retry windowing with jitter, fallback to smaller quantized model), and agreed on a repro for tail latency. Security asked for KMS details and SOC2 evidence. Next steps: repro run, logs from Clearline, pricing/pilot addendum.

Topics covered:
- Incident recap and timeline (Friday 02:14–02:42 UTC)
- Request shaping and rate-windowing concepts
- Retry budgets, client vs server backoff coordination
- KV cache warmup and model variant fallback strategy
- Security/compliance asks for Private run
- Action items and dates

Transcript body:
[00:00] Maya (AE): Hey everyone thanks for joining, we'll run 40 minutes, agenda is quick incident synthesis from Friday, tuning knobs, and then define next steps.
[00:22] Marcus: Thanks Maya, quick reminder — our SLAs are pretty tight at Clearline, the 5xx spike yesterday caused a backlog in our downstream processors so wanted to make sure we cover cause and immediate mitigation.
[00:37] Omar (SE): Yeah we dug into the logs — there's a hotkey surge when a couple of nightly jobs hit the summarization endpoint, tokens per request jumped and we saw KV cache misses when we rotated to the newer quant model. That combination amplified per-token latency leading to timeouts that cascaded into 502/504s at the gateway.
[01:05] Sofia: A few clarifications — when you say "quant model rotate" do you mean you swapped artifact or retrained? The deployment pipeline did a small promote Friday at 02:10.
[01:18] Omar (SE): Right it was a promote to a 4-bit quantized variant to save cost; binary was compatible but the first few warm requests had cold KV and longer kernel fallback paths, we saw 30–50ms extra per token on the long tail.
[01:42] Marcus: We also had a concurrent change on our side — LB health-check window shrank at 02:08 so backend churn and routing flapped for a few minutes, eyeballing the traces they line up.
[01:56] Ethan (Product): So is this mostly warmup related or did the model change increase absolute p95/p99?
[02:08] Omar (SE): Both. Baseline p50 stayed okay but p95/p99 and tail IO spiked. The model variant added jitter to long running inferences when cache miss hit.
[02:22] Priya (Security): From security perspective we need to know if any of that data persisted outside our VPC during retries/fallbacks — were any requests routed to hosted fallbacks?
[02:35] Maya (AE): Good question — during the pilot you're pinned to the private pilot pool, but our fallback routing logic can send to a compatible hosted variant if private capacity is exhausted. For the Friday incident, our telemetry shows 3% of requests were routed to our fallback pool for 6 minutes. We'll produce the exact list — Omar will include routing flags in the repro logs.
[03:02] Marcus: That 3% is the tricky bit for us, we've got PHI concerns. We need either no-hosted fallback or contractual guarantees and encryption-at-rest keys.
[03:18] Lena (CSM): We've done private-only pilots before; Redwood can disable cross-pool fallback per customer while we tune. There is an operational impact but it's doable for the pilot window.
[03:32] Priya (Security): Also send SOC2 report and KMS/HSM architecture doc. We need to sign-off for any hosted fallback.
[03:45] Maya (AE): Will do — I'll attach SOC2 link and an HSM diagram.
[03:50] Omar (SE): For remediation, quick wins: 1) client retry budgeting with exponential backoff + full jitter, capped at 3 retries for idempotent calls; 2) server-side adaptive backpressure — we can drop or deprioritize long-running low-priority requests under surge; 3) pre-warm KV cache for the scheduled jobs using a lightweight probe.
[04:23] Marcus: For the client retry suggestion, our ingestion job is bulk and not idempotent unless we change semantics. Retries will re-send duplicates. How do you recommend dedupe?
[04:38] Omar (SE): Good point — we suggested idempotency tokens for each batch or sequence numbers. Alternatively, have the client checkpoint and resume instead of blind retries.
[04:50] Sofia: Can we throttle the scheduled job to smooth the hourly spike? That might be easier short term.
[04:58] Ethan: We can add a ramping window on the job scheduler yes.
[05:05] Maya (AE): Tactically, the pilot plan: disable hosted fallback for the next 48h, add a warmup probe before scheduled jobs, and run a repro where Redwood generates synthetic burst matching the shape Marcus will provide.
[05:18] Marcus: I'll share the traffic shape and our current LB config by Friday.
[05:24] Omar (SE): For the repro, we'll do three runs: cold cache with model A, warm cache with model A, and model B (4-bit quant) warm/cold to contrast. We'll capture kernel fallbacks, GPU queue lengths, and router 5xx counts.
[05:41] Priya (Security): Also, how do you handle logs with PHI? We need guaranteed redaction and retention policies.
[05:55] Maya (AE): Redwood supports log redaction for pilot customers and configurable retention. We'll share the retention options in the security packet.
[06:05] Omar (SE): One nuance — the router's rate-window is evaluated per-second but with a leaky-bucket overlay; if your job hits a tight burst window (1000 requests in 10s) the windowing may trigger hard rejects rather than smoothing. We recommend smoothing upstream or increasing the burst quota temporarily during the job with Dedicated burst capacity.
[06:30] Marcus: What's the delta to enable a short burst reservation? We don't want to commit long term.
[06:38] Maya (AE): We can add a short-term Dedicated burst addendum for the pilot (billing pro-rated). I'll include numbers in the pricing update.
[06:48] Sofia: If we choose to keep hosted fallback off, what's the failure mode? Do requests queue or return errors?
[06:55] Omar (SE): If we disable fallback and capacity hits, requests will get errors based on your SLA settings — either immediate 429 or timed queue then 504 if queue depth exceeded. We can tune queue depth and circuit-breaker thresholds.
[07:12] Ethan: For user experience we prefer graceful degrade — short error messages vs full failure. Can Redwood return partial answers or cached summaries?
[07:24] Omar (SE): We have a cached prefix strategy and also a smaller model variant that can answer with lower fidelity quickly; we can configure a fallback chain inside the private pool so data never leaves the VPC. That gives graceful degradation without hosted fallback.
[07:40] Marcus: That would be ideal. How much quality drop are we looking at with the quantized smaller variant?
[07:48] Omar (SE): Depends on prompt. For summarization it's usually acceptable; p50 latency drops by ~40% and cost by ~60% but p99 quality regressions are task-specific — we'll produce evals on your prompt set.
[08:05] Maya (AE): Quick check — do we have alignment on the three immediate mitigations? 1) disable hosted fallback for 48h, 2) prewarm probes, 3) repro runs with logs.
[08:18] Marcus: Agreed.
[08:20] Priya: Agreed subject to SOC2 doc and HSM info in writing.
[08:28] Lena (CSM): I'll open a pilot ticket to track the items and owner assignments.
[08:34] Maya (AE): Great. Also we'll share a short runbook for on-call steps if this happens again — a checklist: toggle fallback, increase burst quota, run warmup, and throttle ingestion.
[08:48] Sofia: Can you also add an example curl for the warmup probe? We can schedule it in our cron.
[08:55] Omar (SE): Yep I'll include an example and a small python snippet to warm the KV for a batch of keys.
[09:10] Ethan: On timelines, once we get the logs from Marcus will you be able to repro same-day?
[09:17] Omar (SE): We should be able to repro within 24 hours of traffic shape and LB config.
[09:23] Marcus: I'll drop a link to the trace archive and a short README in the ticket.
[09:30] Maya (AE): Perfect. Any other blockers?
[09:34] Priya: One more on encryption in transit to hosted service — you said fallback used TLS, but do you support customer-managed keys for hosted segments?
[09:45] Maya (AE): For hosted fallback we support TLS in transit; customer-managed keys for storage are supported on Private but hosted fallback uses Redwood-managed keys by default. We'll propose options in the compliance packet — HSM + BYOK options for Private deployments and contract language for hosted fallbacks.
[09:58] Marcus: Ok appreciate that clarity.
[10:02] Maya (AE): Cool, wrap up — Omar will kick off the repro, Marcus will share traces, Priya will confirm compliance blockers, Maya will send pricing and SOC2 link. Lena will track the ticket. We'll reconvene after the repro — propose Friday standup 10:00 PT to review results.
[10:28] Marcus: Sounds good, thanks all.
[10:33] Maya (AE): Thanks everyone.
